Perth · WA · Family Home Model · Confidential to the buyer

Buying near Como, without buying the top.

A scenario-based house-price model and suburb-targeting study for one buyer: a family home within reach of Como (6152), $1.0M to spend ($200k equity + $800k at 0% interest), patient enough to wait for the 2027 soft patch.

Anchored to family in Como 6152 · 3-year primary horizon, 5-year tail · as at mid-2026

Executive summary

The most accurate approach for a single-city, suburb-level, ≤5-year horizon is a four-layer hybrid: a city-level error-correction (VECM) spine that anchors price to fundamentals, driving a scenario-weighted Monte Carlo fan, with a suburb gradient-boosted panel and a hedonic property layer on top. Pure machine learning alone is least reliable beyond ~12 months. A 3-year primary horizon (with a 5-year scenario tail) is optimal because forecast error compounds and the buyer's decision window — the 2027 soft patch — sits inside three years.

The mid-2026 macro state validates the thesis but argues for a slightly cautious base case. Perth is expensive and decelerating yet structurally undersupplied, so a 2014-style crash is unlikely. The real risk is a resources-led soft patch (iron ore easing, the Simandou ramp, and an investor-demand headwind from the 1 July 2027 negative-gearing/CGT change) — and it lines up with the buyer's window. With $800k at 0%, waiting is nearly free, so the play is patience plus the right suburbs.

Where to buy — the shortlist

Premium river suburbs are out of budget for a house (Como ~$1.5M+, South Perth ~$2.0M, Applecross ~$2.4M). The play is the fringe of the best school catchments and near-in Canning value. At the balanced setting the model ranks Shelley #1, Wilson #2.

What makes this model different — enriched, leading variables

A generic model stops at rates, migration and approvals. This one adds family-buyer-specific leading indicators and a cyclical-risk overlay that explain which suburbs hold up through the soft patch.

VariableTierWhat it predicts (leads price by)Source

School in-zone rejection eventsACatchment premium spilling to fringe suburbsWA Education intake + ACARA

FIFO-share × iron-ore interactionBSuburb mining-cashflow beta (5-yr tail risk)ATO postcode × commodity

The buyer's "child rates" hint is correct and is operationalised fast→slow via pool permits, childcare occupancy, school-zone pressure, and SA2 family-cohort share. The discipline: permit/register/roster data leads; demographic counts lag — never let a slow series move a near-term call alone.

Recommendations & timing

Posture

  • Patient / opportunistic — the $800k-at-0% facility removes the carrying cost of waiting.
  • Primary targets: Shelley, Wilson, St James, Parkwood, Bentley; secondary north-of-river land (Dianella, Embleton, Balcatta).
  • Highest conviction hold: Rossmoyne-catchment fringe — scarce land + family demand + grandfathered owner-occupier status.

Act when any two confirm a soft patch

  • Perth monthly growth flat/negative for 2+ months.
  • Advertised stock rising toward the 5-year average.
  • Iron ore sustained <US$85/t with rising FIFO unemployment.
  • Days-on-market past ~20 in target suburbs.

Data, reproducibility & the live tool

The forecast is reproducible — the standard-library Python in /model regenerates these exact baseline numbers and self-verifies. The interactive web tool (single self-contained HTML, published to GitHub Pages) lets the buyer drag scenario weights and a proximity-vs-schools slider, with a Reset button that restores this model's prescribed baseline exactly, plus a suburb heat map and pre-filtered live saved-search links to the property portals. A genuinely refreshing listings feed is available via the compliant Domain Developer API path (scheduled job → data/listings.json) — never by scraping.

General information only — not financial, legal or tax advice. All figures are approximations as at mid-2026 and will change. Suburb medians vary 10–20% between sources and are shown as ranges; no public source publishes median block size, so the 450sqm requirement must be confirmed per-listing via Landgate. The forecast is a set of scenario estimates conditioned on the stated assumptions and will be wrong if those assumptions are wrong (a global shock, an iron-ore collapse below ~US$70, or a migration reversal are the things that break it). Verify against live REIWA, Landgate, RBA and ABS data and licensed professionals before acting. Generated by the Como-Anchored Perth Home Model.
